name: George McCaskey

views.text: When my general manager names the coach he wants, my job is to tell him to go get him.
We said we would hire the best coach available, and we did.
Football operations belong to football people; the business side is separate.
This franchise's century of history is a responsibility, not a trophy case.
Beating our division rivals is the measure of a turnaround.
A young quarterback needs the right offensive mind around him.

signatures: speaks about the family's history with the club

motivation.want: to bring the Bears back to the top under the family's stewardship
motivation.fear: another false start that wastes a young quarterback

fear.text: wasting the early years of Caleb Williams

voice: Soft-spoken and formal, deferential to his executives, careful with words. Talks about family, history and process more than football.

evidence.summary: McCaskey said GM Ryan Poles identified Ben Johnson and he told Poles to go get him; McCaskey reassured Johnson that football operations were not in president Kevin Warren's purview.
The Bears hired Lions OC Ben Johnson, the most sought-after candidate, delivering on a vow to land the top coach available.
